How does segmentation differ from isolation
Option1: Segmentation limits access by dividing networks while isolation completely separates systems
Option2: Isolation uses software while segmentation uses hardware
Option3: Segmentation encrypts data while isolation prevents access
Option4: Isolation is used only in virtual machines

Q: What is the key difference between access control and permissions
Option1: Permissions apply to specific resources while access control defines overall access policies
Option2: Access control encrypts traffic while permissions block users
Option3: Permissions are for external users while access control is for internal users
Option4: Both terms mean the same in practice

Q: How does an access control list differ from an application allow list
Option1: Access control list defines who can access what resources while application allow list limits which software can run
Option2: Application allow list controls ports while access control list blocks domains
Option3: Access control list uses encryption while allow list uses hashing
Option4: Both are part of configuration enforcement

Q: Why are permissions not sufficient without proper configuration enforcement
Option1: Permissions require enforcement mechanisms to be effective
Option2: Permissions encrypt data while enforcement blocks access
Option3: Enforcement is only used in mobile devices

Q: How does an application allow list differ from a blacklist
Option1: Application allow list permits only approved software while a blacklist blocks specific known threats
Option2: Application allow list scans files while blacklist blocks traffic
Option3: Blacklist encrypts data while allow list hides it

Q: Why is isolation considered stronger than segmentation in some cases
Option1: Isolation completely disconnects systems while segmentation still allows limited communication
Option2: Segmentation encrypts traffic while isolation does not
Option4: Segmentation applies only to physical networks

Q: How is patching different from hardening
Option1: Patching updates software to fix vulnerabilities while hardening configures systems to reduce attack surfaces
Option2: Patching blocks access while hardening applies firewall rules
Option3: Both are methods of access control

Q: What is the relationship between encryption and data confidentiality
Option1: Encryption ensures confidentiality by making data unreadable without the correct key

Q: How does monitoring differ from access control
Option1: Monitoring detects and logs activity while access control determines who can do what
Option4: Monitoring is only useful after a breach

Q: How does least privilege support overall security
Option1: It limits access rights to only what is needed which reduces the impact of a compromise
Option2: It grants full access to administrators
Option4: It only applies to encryption keys

Q: What distinguishes configuration enforcement from patch management
Option1: Configuration enforcement ensures settings stay compliant while patch management updates software
Option2: Patch management only applies to firewalls
Option3: Configuration enforcement is used only in testing

Q: How is decommissioning different from disabling ports and protocols
Option1: Decommissioning removes a system entirely while disabling ports and protocols reduces its attack surface
Option4: Disabling ports applies only to wireless networks

Q: What is the main purpose of hardening in enterprise environments
Option1: To reduce vulnerabilities through multiple defensive configurations
Option3: To ensure user credentials are reused
Option4: To isolate encrypted data from firewalls

Q: How does encryption as a hardening technique differ from general encryption
Option1: In hardening it is applied system-wide to protect critical data and functions
Option3: Hardening encryption is only for mobile devices

Q: How does endpoint protection differ from host-based firewalls
Option1: Endpoint protection includes antivirus and malware defense while firewalls filter traffic
Option2: Firewalls monitor applications but endpoint protection blocks ports
Option3: Endpoint protection is only used in routers

Q: What sets host-based firewalls apart from network firewalls
Option1: Host-based firewalls protect individual systems while network firewalls guard traffic between systems

Q: Why is a host-based intrusion prevention system considered proactive
Option1: It can block threats before they execute based on behavior analysis
Option4: It replaces all access control rules

Q: How does disabling ports and protocols enhance system security
Option1: It reduces the number of entry points for attackers by limiting unnecessary services

Q: Why is changing default passwords a crucial security step
Option1: Default credentials are widely known and often targeted by attackers
Option2: They cannot be changed once set

Q: How does removal of unnecessary software contribute to system hardening
Option1: It reduces the attack surface by eliminating unneeded applications that may contain vulnerabilities
